title: Kitchen Drain Maintenance: Preventing Grease Buildup
description: An educational guide demonstrating how fats, oils, and grease (FOG) solidify inside kitchen sink P-traps and branch lines, and how proper preventative maintenance preserves drain flow.
image_prompt: A professional educational technical cutaway illustration of a kitchen sink drainage system inside a cabinet, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. The image clearly features a 1.5-inch white plastic tubular P-trap connected beneath a stainless steel kitchen sink basin. A clean cross-section cutaway of the P-trap wall reveals a realistic layer of yellowish congealed grease lining the bottom interior curve of the trap arm, showing how grease reduces the internal diameter of the pipe. Realistically rendered clean wastewater passes through the center. Studio educational lighting, neutral wall background, realistic plumbing fittings including slip-nut connections and rubber washers visible in section. Main P-trap assembly centered with ample clean space at top and bottom for text overlays. Physically accurate plumbing geometry, photorealistic textures. No text, no labels, no watermarks, no logos, no fake branding.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway section of a standard kitchen P-trap to show the physical mechanism of drain restriction. Viewers can see how liquid fats, which enter the sink warm, cool down and solidify along the pipe walls, gradually choking water flow over time. This makes the invisible problem inside household piping immediately visible and understandable.

on_image_text.explanation: Warm liquid fats cool down inside uninsulated pipes, solidifying along the inner walls.
on_image_text.callout: FOG (Fats, Oils & Grease) Accumulation inside P-Trap
on_image_text.takeaway: Scrape pans into trash before washing; flush regularly with hot water and dish soap.
